OUTSIDE IMAGING REPORT
Exam: Ultrasound, abdomen complete.
Indication: Primary sclerosing cholangitis, rising bilirubin.
Findings: The intrahepatic bile ducts are beaded and irregular. The liver is normal in size without focal mass. Gallbladder is normal, without stones or wall thickening. Visualized pancreas unremarkable. Spleen normal in size. Both kidneys normal in size without hydronephrosis. Abdominal aorta normal caliber. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Beading and irregularity of the intrahepatic bile ducts, consistent with known primary sclerosing cholangitis.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Follow-up
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY GROUP
Date of service: 04/20/2026
Re: Austin Crowley, DOB 04/05/1992

Dear Doctor,

Austin returned six months after we diagnosed primary sclerosing cholangitis. Fatigue and itching have persisted through the winter and he has been yellow off and on. Over the last stretch he has noticed pale stools and dark urine. His colitis has stayed quiet on mesalamine, and the bleeding episodes he described last fall have not come back.

Medications: mesalamine DR 1.2 g twice daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: maternal grandmother UC, father PSC, mother autoimmune hypothyroidism.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, financial analyst.

Exam: afebrile. Sclerae icteric. Abdomen soft, not distended, no masses, mildly tender in the right upper quadrant.

Labs 04/20/2026:
Total bilirubin 3.2 mg/dL (H)
Direct bilirubin 2.5 mg/dL (H)
Alkaline phosphatase 420 U/L (H)
AST 80 U/L (H)
ALT 75 U/L (H)
CA 19-9 22 U/mL (normal)

Abdominal ultrasound today: beaded, irregular intrahepatic ducts (report enclosed).

Impression: PSC with worsening cholestasis and jaundice; concern for a dominant stricture. CA 19-9 reassuring.
Plan: ERCP with cholangiography, possible dilation and brushings, being scheduled at the regional hospital. Continue mesalamine.

Thank you for allowing us to share in his care.

Gastroenterology

reports.text:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL ENDOSCOPY
Procedure: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography with biliary balloon dilation and brushings.
Indication: Primary sclerosing cholangitis with rising bilirubin, pale stools and dark urine.
Sedation: Monitored anesthesia care.
Findings: Normal major papilla. Deep biliary cannulation achieved. Cholangiogram shows multifocal intrahepatic strictures with intervening dilation, and a dominant stricture of the common bile duct. Biliary sphincterotomy not performed. The dominant stricture was dilated with a balloon. Brushings of the stricture sent for cytology. Good drainage of contrast after dilation. No stent placed. Pancreatic duct not opacified.
Complications: None.
Disposition: Discharged home the same day.
reports.conclusion: Dominant common bile duct stricture in primary sclerosing cholangitis, balloon dilated; brushings obtained; no stent.

documents.body:
Regional hospital endoscopy report, procedure date 05/12/2026, received by fax.

ERCP for PSC with worsening cholestasis. Dominant common bile duct stricture identified and balloon dilated; brushings sent to cytology. No stent. No complications. Discharged home same day with his family. Mesalamine to continue. Clinic follow-up with labs in about six weeks.

Allergies: NKDA.

reports.text:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL PATHOLOGY
Specimen: Common bile duct stricture, brushings.
Clinical history: Primary sclerosing cholangitis, dominant stricture.
Adequacy: Satisfactory for evaluation.
Microscopic: Cellular specimen with benign ductal epithelium in flat sheets. No atypical or malignant cells identified.

documents.body: Cytology report from the regional hospital for the 05/12/2026 ERCP brushings: benign ductal cells, negative for malignancy. Copy also sent to ordering gastroenterologist. Scanned to chart. -- MA

documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY GROUP
Date of service: 06/22/2026
Re: Austin Crowley, DOB 04/05/1992

Dear Doctor,

Follow-up six weeks after ERCP with balloon dilation of a dominant common bile duct stricture (brushings benign). Austin feels much better. The itching has largely settled, his stools are a normal color again and his urine is no longer dark. Colitis remains quiet on mesalamine.

Medications: mesalamine DR 1.2 g twice daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: anicteric. Abdomen soft and nontender.

Labs 06/22/2026:
Total bilirubin 1.4 mg/dL (H)
Direct bilirubin 0.8 mg/dL (H)
Alkaline phosphatase 310 U/L (H)
AST 48 U/L (H)
ALT 52 U/L

Impression: PSC, improved biochemically and clinically after stricture dilation.
Plan: continue mesalamine 1.2 g twice daily. Hepatic panel and CA 19-9 in late August; he may have them drawn at your office. Repeat MRCP in about a year. Return to clinic in the fall.

Thank you for allowing us to share in his care.

Gastroenterology
